claims.text: Brent crude futures rose $1.24 to $106.93 a barrel on Tuesday following attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure.
U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose $1.29 to $102.65 a barrel on Tuesday.
Houthi forces launched a missile and drone attack targeting aircraft hangars and ammunition depots at the Khamis Mushait military airbase in southern Saudi Arabia on Monday.
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline transports oil across the country to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, allowing exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
Commodity vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to fewer than 10 per day over the weekend, compared to a 10-day average of 14.
The Saudi-led coalition stated that 13 civilians were injured in Saudi Arabia following a wave of ballistic missile and drone attacks by Houthi forces.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that Iran will not enter talks with the United States until Tehran's conditions are met.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree stated that Saudi warplanes carried out 58 air raids across six provinces within a 24-hour period.

U.S. Central Command rejected Iranian claims that the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia hit a naval mine, stating it was struck by an Iranian drone off the coast of Oman over the weekend after being hit by an Iranian missile last month.
Thirteen of the 14 Indian crew members aboard the oil tanker El Gaia were rescued off the coast of Oman, while one Indian crew member remained missing.
Tehran imposed a virtual blockade on the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026 following U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran on February 28.
Brent crude surged to more than $108.50 a barrel on Monday, representing a 3.7 percent daily increase.
The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds reached 5 percent on Monday, marking its highest level since October 2023.
Iran-aligned Houthi forces captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday.
U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Ukraine and Russia agreed not to strike each other's energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is willing to halt strikes on Russian critical infrastructure if Russia stops its attacks on Ukrainian energy targets.
European Union member states extended the deadline for renewing sanctions against Russia by one week following a push by France to remove Uzbek-Russian tycoon Alisher Usmanov from the blacklist.
A member of the British armed forces died in a non-hostile road traffic incident in Ukraine on Saturday.
A Russian drone struck Yahodyn train station near the Polish border on Sunday shortly after a train carrying former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson departed.
Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Ukrainian president's office, stated that Ukraine is preparing for a new round of US-mediated trilateral talks with Russia in October.
A summer 2026 poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology found that 60 percent of Ukrainians support freezing frontline fighting in exchange for security guarantees.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte pledged increased support for Ukraine and strengthened defenses along NATO's eastern border following Russian drone strikes near Poland.
Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz stated that the Polish military recovered a suspected Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea near Jaroslawiec.
Russian forces struck two cargo vessels in the Black Sea on Monday, according to reports from Interfax.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay titled 'We Must Pace the Frontier' urging a slowdown in artificial intelligence development.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk expressed support for Dario Amodei's call to slow AI development.
U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed efforts to regulate artificial intelligence, posting that calls for guardrails are a 'sick conspiracy'.
Shares in Nvidia fell 3.3 percent and SoftBank stock slumped 13 percent on Monday following tech leaders' public warnings regarding AI safety.
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC that a third-party AI 'kill switch' may be required to prevent potential catastrophes.
Anthropic and OpenAI filed SEC documentation one week apart to list on public markets at target valuations exceeding $1 trillion.
OpenAI and Google signed agreements with the U.S. Pentagon in February 2026 after Anthropic refused to allow its AI models to be used for autonomous lethal weapons or mass surveillance.
Elon Musk's X Corp and SpaceXAI dropped their antitrust claims against Apple over its ChatGPT integration while continuing their lawsuit against OpenAI.
X Corp and SpaceXAI filed an antitrust lawsuit in August 2025 alleging Apple and OpenAI colluded to make ChatGPT the exclusive AI chatbot integrated into the iPhone operating system.
Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote launched an initial public offering for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery seeking to raise $1.6 billion from retail investors across Africa.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO offers retail investors a minimum 10-share bundle for 5,250 naira ($4).
Aliko Dangote will retain an 87 percent ownership stake in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery following the public offering.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery supplies more than 70 percent of Nigeria's domestic energy consumption.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery generated an after-tax profit of $1.82 billion in the first half of 2026 after posting a $476 million loss in 2025.
Dangote Industries plans to use funds raised from the IPO to support a $14.3 billion expansion aimed at increasing refining capacity from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day.
Aliko Dangote plans to launch an oil processing plant in Kenya in partnership with eastern African governments.
The initial public offering for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery opened on the Nigerian exchange with subscription running until October 13.
Aliko Dangote plans to build a $17 billion energy complex in Lamu, Kenya, with a refining capacity of 700,000 barrels per day.

Scottish First Minister John Swinney, Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth, and Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Cardiff calling for independence from the United Kingdom.
Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald signed the Cardiff memorandum alongside the first ministers of Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
Plaid Cymru's victory in the May Senedd elections ended Labour's continuous governance of Wales that began with devolution in 1999.
Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross characterized the Cardiff meeting as a 'separatist summit' and a 'performative photo call'.
Downing Street stated that UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is focused on tackling the cost-of-living crisis rather than engaging in constitutional debates.
The joint statement signed by the SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Sinn Féin declared that Europe is their common home and that the future of their nations belongs in the European Union.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham rejected calls to hold another Scottish independence referendum before the next general election.
